conviction_note: H1 FY27 numbers are new (only 'solid start' was said in September) and the FY27 guide is exposed to two unquantified risks (post-duty vaping, Poundland), so abs_move is set at 7.5 on thin turnover and one analyst; the findings roughly offset (sum +0.1) and p_up is pulled to 47 because this name has fallen on 4 of its last 5 results days, which is why the scaled number (-0.45) sits slightly below the findings sum.

new_in_release.expect: H1 FY27 revenue and adj EBITDA are new. Expect H1 EBITDA above the GBP18.5m of H1 FY26, from a full half of SlimFast and probable pre-duty vaping sell-in in September. Up, but largely inside the FY guide.
FY27 'in line with expectations' most likely reiterated. A trim is the main downside risk (Vaping Products Duty volumes from 1 Oct, Poundland lost sales). Unknown sign; the size of the move is here.
First post-duty trading commentary for October and November. Unknown. The one external proxy says consumer vape volumes normalised close to pre-duty levels in October.
Quantification of the Poundland impact (receivable write-off, at most about GBP0.5m, plus lost sales). Mildly negative.
Interim dividend; 1.6p last year under a 25%-of-PAT policy. Likely flat to up. Low weight.
Net cash/working capital after a likely pre-duty inventory or receivables swing at 30 Sept. Unknown.

findings.finding: One independent retail series shows vape volumes pulled forward into September ahead of the 1 Oct duty (daily sales +50% across September, e-liquids +78%, peak +390% on 30 Sept), then returning to about 1% below the June-July average from 3 to 31 October. That points to a September-boosted H1 vaping line and a less damaging first post-duty month than the 18% de-rating implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Vaping-regulation prints: H1 FY26 (disposable ban navigated, EBITDA flat) fell 6.55%; FY26 finals (flat EBITDA, vape margin pressure) fell 6.41%. The stock has not rewarded 'resilience' language.
findings.why_not_priced: It is one online specialist's data, published a week before the print in the trade press. Supreme has said nothing since 17 Sept on post-duty trading, and the stock has fallen steadily (-17.9% over 60 days, -8.6% over 20) with no company news other than Poundland. If the market had read October as normalised, the slide would not have continued into November.
findings.independence: Both halves come from one document (Vape and Go via Retail Times), so they are merged here into one finding. The company's own September view that 88Vape's value positioning will resonate under the duty (https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/supreme-ceo-confident-in-face-of-vaping-dutys-blow-to-margins/723719.article) is management opinion, not data.

findings.finding: Poundland, a named Supreme customer, filed notice to appoint administrators (Supreme RNS 30 Oct 2026). Net receivables exposure is GBP460k, and Supreme said the impact on future profitability could not yet be quantified, with a 'further update in due course' that the interims are the natural place for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior customer-insolvency event at Supreme on record. The stock went from 132p (22 Oct) to 121.6p (23 Nov), part of which is this news.
findings.original_quote: Given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Poundland's future trading arrangements and the extent of its retail estate, it is not yet possible to reliably quantify the potential impact on the Group's future profitability.
findings.why_not_priced: The receivable is known and tiny (about 1% of FY EBITDA). The lost-sales effect on the FY27 guide is explicitly unquantified, and Poundland's outcome (whole-business buyer versus a break-up of the roughly 600 stores) was still unresolved in public reporting, so the market cannot have priced the number Supreme will give. The decline since the notice suggests some haircut is already in.
findings.independence: Press reports of the 29 Oct High Court filing and the sale process (https://www.cityam.com/?p=2472970) confirm the counterparty event, not Supreme's exposure.

findings.finding: H1 FY27 carries a full half of SlimFast (acquired October 2025, after H1 FY26 closed), which Supreme said together with 1001 adds about GBP6.5m of annualised adj EBITDA. On a like-for-like reading the H1 headline should exceed the GBP18.5m of H1 FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26 grew revenue 17% on acquisitions with flat EBITDA and fell 6.55%. Acquisition-driven top-line growth has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The acquisition is public and sits inside the FY27 consensus the company says it is tracking. It matters only for how the H1 headline reads, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: The prior-year interim (H1 FY26 adj EBITDA GBP18.5m, SlimFast acquired post-period in October) gives the comparison base: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/supreme--sup/half-year-results/9254581

findings.finding: The CEO (54.69% holder) bought 500,000 shares at 131.811p on 20 July 2026, about 8% above the sealed spot.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it is four months old. Filed because it is a sourced insider signal ahead of the half, and the stock has since fallen below his entry.

outside_window.finding: Unstamped pre-duty vape stock can be sold until 31 March 2027, so retailer destocking of September sell-in may weigh on H2 FY27 vaping orders. This will show in the March trading update, not in this window except through guidance commentary.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.43) is just the bounce prior from a -8.6% 20-day run-up. The findings roughly offset rather than cutting against it, and the name's own history of selling results days pulls the other way.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: the domestic UK sources (Investegate RNS, LSE news, The Grocer, Retail Times) were the primary sources throughout, and the international wire/sell-side layer carried nothing on this one-analyst AIM name
lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': the September stockpiling and October normalisation findings (both Vape and Go via Retail Times) merged into one at +0.5
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the merged vape finding was kept at +0.5 rather than +1.0, since it is a single online retailer's data
'The move is in the guide' plus 'too small about the move': H1 is not pre-released and a guide change is possible, so abs_move went from 6.0 to 7.5 (thin, one analyst)
'Reaction history vetoes the direction, not the size': the name fell on 4 of its last 5 results days, so p_up went from 50 to 47 and abs was not cut
Finding inside the guide toward 0: SlimFast full-half contribution cut from +0.3 to +0.2; Poundland cut from -0.8 to -0.7 because part of it is already in the post-notice decline
